Great place to visit, both educational and fun. its really impressive to see all the unique creatures that live in the ocean. dedicate at least several hours to the visit. || This place gets it!  It's all about the service and people.  Incredibly helpful and friendly staff.  Very clean place.  Food was good and fair priced.  The exhibits were all well maintained.  Especially with children, this is a very nice all day activity. || We’ve been to aquariums all over the world and this isn’t the glossiest or the most high tech. But my kids love it and beg to come back every time we are in Eilat. There’s lots of different things to do that keep everyone entertained and you cannot beat seeing fish in their actual habitat. We love this charming little place. The 3-D movie was a huge hit! || What a great chance to sit and watch fish for hours! Between the underwater observatory and the aquarium we were really pleased with the experience.  Go early for quieter viewing without crowds. There was plenty of parking when they first opened. || We spent the whole day, ~7 hours, so there's lots to do there. I won't give it a 5 star since some things definitely need more love. We saw all the exhibits, there's really a good wide variety and selection of sea creatures, most endemic to Eilat. The highlight must be the shark tank, it has multiple viewing windows, plenty of room, probably the nicest tank I've seen. They feed them twice daily - go to the second feeding! (3pm) it far less crowded. There's a tube to walk under the fish and rays, beautiful. There are also turtles and "rare creatures" (which we didn't find very "rare"). The "deep sea creatures" exhibit is only videos. The lowest point must be the "IMAX", the movie is short, although the 3D effect is cool (kids loved it), but the narration (Heb only) is unintelligible, the content is boring, and they play a "generic" 3D flick. The underwater structure is very nice, but many windows are way too high for a 3-4 y/o to see anything without carrying them 💪, still it's very worth the while (climb up to see the overlook). It's a good place to spend a few hours, it doesn't break the bank, and kids will like it. || Great place to visit. Easy to get to by bus from Eilat. You can buy tickets online or at the gate. The exhibits are lovely.. sharks, stingrays, corals, turtles, octopi, fish. Climb the observatory to the top to see great views of the Red Sea.. then go below sea level to view coral and fish. Try and avoid Jewish / school holidays is it gets very busy. The 3D movie was an extra .. it was not so good.

We came 5 mins after 12pm (and tickets are valid also tomorrow from the morning only! - as explained on the cash desk); spent some half day here late March; sea temperature fresh but still acceptable; not so crowded today; beach service collect beach chairs regularly; easy to find place and take chairs, we enjoy hot and cold sweets with coffee and fresh Mint lemonade. Really tasty; recommended; next time I repeat. || Amazing ! Such an incredible experience ! Staff are also amazing ! Estelle was great called me told me best times to come ! Mayaan was so welcoming and beautiful and IRa was amazing guide ! She was brilliant and supported me on my first dive ! Dolphins are everywhere ❤️❤️ || For the standard entrance fee you can swim at the beach and spend some time on the pier to film and shoot the dolphins (pier closes at 5 pm). Then you have a bar restaurant upstairs in a wonderful place (forbidden under 18 years old). From this place you still can see the dolphins, enjoy the sun and even stay until 11 pm! || Great place. We did snorkeling with the dolphins, it was great to see them in their natural habitat. Our instructor was a very nice and professional lady that took care of everyone’s comfort and made sure everyone is safe and have an amazing time. I was really scared of the depth but thanks to her I could overcome my fear and enjoy the moment. I can’t thank her enough. It’s a place one of a kind and people there are very welcoming. I highly recommend, worth every penny. || I had a great expirience to dive with dolphins..its something amazing..also the place its like heaven..its diferent than other places that i saw in Israel. The relaxing pools inside its something special too. I recommand everyone to visit. || Wonderful location, really worth the detour even though it's located on the other side of Eilat. There's also a bar inside where you can order drinks and bites. Service was great and the food was delicious. A big 5! || Very clean beach and not too crowded. Dolphins seem happy and free. Very good diving guides, and great service. They even offered us a refund for  for one who couldn't make it on time, because they had another person who was interested to dive instead. || Very beautiful dolphin reef. Tourist attraction. We saw 3 dolphins. The food here was delicious, totally recommend! There are also student fares for entry. || Dolphin Reef in Eilat is a natural habitat of Dolphins. We can observe the dolphins 🐬 from the floating bridge provided. The dolphins are very playful and you are allowed to touch them if you wish to.  The security staff watches over the dolphins as well as feeds them.Some snorkeling facility is also there. We visited long back. The Dolphin Reef is open from Monday to Saturday.  Timings: 9 am to 5 pm. We spent some time observing the dolphins.  There is an entry fee. || The most wonderful beach in Eilat. It’s like a completely different world everything beautiful and clean and pleasant. The food at the beach restaurant is great. And to watch the dolphins is certainly a bonus 🐬 …

The Best Hotel in Eilat for kids!!!!!! There is no other hotel that will take it from U koral beach. Just bring your kid in the morning to the entertainment crew and your kid will be busy all day - amazing! Yes, it pretty far from the main city, but you have everything in the hotel, even beach nearby. I will come back next year! || Thank you so much for your wonderful review! We’re delighted to hear you enjoyed your stay and we look forward to welcoming you back again soon. 🌞 … || I have visited this resort 4 times over the past 27 years (three times in the past five years) and am always happy to return there. The staff are friendly and attentive, the location is excellent - within walking distance of tennis courts, … || I have stayed at U Coral Beach Club multiple times in the past few years with my wife. Overall, it remains one of the most activity-rich hotels in Eilat, but the standards decline each year and might no longer fully justify the price.  Room cleanliness was disappointing. We were upgraded from a Superior U room (the most basic category) to a balcony room, but the upgrade was not worthwhile. Last time we stayed in the Superior U room, and to me it felt newer, cleaner, and had a much nicer bathroom than the balcony room. The balcony room’s bathroom was very small, with a combined tub/shower and only a half glass partition, so water splashed everywhere. The Superior U bathroom, while shower-only, is more spacious and modern. In the balcony room, the tub felt old and not properly cleaned, there was hair on the bed, the sofa bed was opened without request, and there was no water or welcome package in the room..  I would not recommend staying during a storm. Check the weather! The power went out for about half an hour, and roads into and out of Eilat were closed. Reception handled this well and graciously offered us an additional night at a slightly discounted rate (around 10%), which we declined. Instead, they offered a complimentary dinner pass, which was much appreciated.  The food remains a strong point. Dinner was excellent, with a wide and impressive variety: steaks, asado, pulled beef bao buns, schnitzel, chicken dishes, and more. The variety is consistently very good. Breakfast, however, was underwhelming. Limited selection, poor pastries, mediocre orange juice, and only black and green tea available.  The dairy restaurant is very good, but availability is limited to certain days and requires first-come, first-served sign-up. Arriving early is essential.  Unlimited cocktails are fun, but the bar offering is basic. Mostly straight liquors with fruit juices. The slushies are extremely sweet and artificial. Bartender skill varies significantly, though one bartender managed to make a decent piña colada. Drinks are always served in plastic cups, though glass cups can be requested at the indoor bar.  Snorkel rentals and beach equipment are excellent. However, windsurfing is advertised but never seems to happen. On multiple visits there has always been an excuse. This time we were told the instructor had passed away...  I would go again, mainly because no other hotel in Eilat offers this level of activities and programming. That said, for the price, cleanliness, room quality, and overall standards should be higher. || We had the best weekend ever! The bridge too the beach is amazing,food was more than expected so much verity options in every meal! The view from the room was breathtaking, it was fun n relaxing.. thank you || Thank you so much for your wonderful feedback! We’re delighted to hear that you had such an amazing weekend and enjoyed the easy beach access, the rich variety of food, and the beautiful room view. It’s great to know your stay was both fun and relaxing. We truly appreciate your kind words! || We have been guests of this hotel for the best part of 20 years already from when it was Club Med, sometimes just the 2 of us, at other times with our family of 8 to 10. The quality … || I left something behind, I feel so bad because it was my favourite to play with. It smells a little, but I promise it’s friendly. Don’t forget to feed it. It’s called “Nigel” please shout his name because he’s hard of hearing. He’s shy so could only one person look for him. Thank you. You are all so lovely. I will come back in 2 days please find him 💔 || Thank you so much for your wonderful review! We’re delighted to hear you enjoyed your stay and we look forward to welcoming you back again soon. 🌞 … || Our stay at Club Inn Eilat was a nightmare from start to finish. The room was neglected and filthy, with peeling walls and a constant smell of mold and dampness. The bathroom was covered with mold – absolutely unacceptable for a hotel, more … || For those who want to save on shopping and dining out  -U coral beach is the perfect place.5 meals -breakfast,dinner,coffee and cake,supper,pizza stand at night,free bar from 9 till 00,entertaining programs for grown ups and kids-so no need … || Huge Thanks to U Coral Beach!  We stayed at U Coral Beach and left with the best impression possible—mostly thanks to the incredible and caring staff.  The welcome was warm and professional. The reception team—just amazing! Polite, patient, and genuinely respectful towards guests. Every request was met promptly and with a smile, every question received an immediate answer, as if they were just waiting to assist.  The rooms were clean, tidy, and equipped with everything you need. And if something was missing, we only had to ask,...It was there. The attention to detail was evident at every turn.  A special thank-you to Pnina, who takes care of guests with allergies. Her attitude was exceptional, straight from the heart. Even on our departure day, she made sure we had sweet surprises and everything we needed for the journey.  The hotel runs on an “all-inclusive” basis, and we’d say—“all-inclusive plus”! Delicious, diverse, clean, and always served with courtesy.  We can’t forget to mention the U Eataly restaurant—part of the package, but it felt like a true bonus! The waitstaff—simply outstanding: polite, quick, and making you feel like a VIP. Even if you’re not a huge fan of Italian cuisine, once you taste it here, you’ll fall in love. We had lunch there and couldn’t make it to dinner.  The hotel offers activities for the whole family—kids, adults, evening shows—it’s all just wonderful.  The lobby bar and the pool bar are always available—hot drinks, cold drinks, whatever you need. And the staff—oh, their patience! With kids, and… let’s just say, with some adults too.  We also want to highlight how the management treats the staff. We witnessed a situation with a guest complaint (let’s be honest—every hotel has them), and we were impressed by how professionally and compassionately it was handled. The manager showed respect both to the guest and to the junior staff member, supporting her while politely resolving the issue. It was very impressive.  U Coral Beach, everything was fantastic! Thank you for an amazing vacation. We will definitely come back! || dear guests Thanks for the support on the site, We are happy to know that you enjoyed your stay We were happy to host you and would love to see you again soon welcome Hotel staff

Ok, this is very good hotel, but the reviews are in need of a correction. This is not the 5-star experience that the internet says it is. 4-stars is much more reasonable.  We stayed there for two nights at the end of 2025. This was certainly a 5-star hotel when it was built around 25 years ago and it's been impressively very well maintained since. But, it's also well overdue for renovation, and 4-stars is a much more reasonable assessment at what it is now. (I gave it 3-stars in this review, just to try to get some balance back in the world.) The difference it makes isn't how nice it is (it's a very good hotel), it's in whether it is worth the price premium. (In my opinion, it is not.)  Here's what you need to know. - Rooms: we stayed in a regular room, which is impressively spacious, but in need of renovation to maintain a 5-star level. The Nespresso machine didn't work and the safe needed a battery. Ok, these things happen. The bed was nice, but not quite as nice as you should get for 5-stars. (It was solid 4-stars.) The bathroom was nice when it was built. It has a jacuzzi but it's not big enough to really use, and the bath leaks a bit. The fridge is old, and the carpeting and doors appear to be original. For this price point, the rooms are well overdue for a renovation.  - Meals: we loved the breakfast and the free snack bar in the afternoon. At breakfast they serve you coffee and eggs which is a substantial upgrade from having to fight your way through a hotel breakfast buffet. We had dinner their one night which was "ok" but not worth the premium. The food was fine, but there is no vibe at all. Also, the service was... odd... they ran out of wine (who runs out of wine?) and I needed to convince them to open a bottle of the "free wine" from the afternoon snack bar instead. They charged me the full price for the "free wine" which was just plain tacky. (Just to be clear, there is a reason why the "free wine" is free. No one should be paying for that experience whether in the afternoon or at dinner.) In any case, I wouldn't go back for the dinners, there are much better options (with much better vibe) outside of the hotel.  - Gym: the gym was built 25 years ago and still has the same equipment. Now, before you freak out about that - wow! Who can maintain equipment that long? It is the absolute perfect setting for a filming a gym scene in Stranger Things. Seriously, if you own this hotel and are reading this: there is no excuse for not having a full gym renovation. (And you should be able to get a good price for collectors of antique weight machines.)  - Spa: we made our final day into a spa day and it was sublime. The facilities are in excellent condition, and include: a very large indoor jacuzzi (great!), a large sauna (great!), a large steam room (great!) as well an outdoor jacuzzi (great!) and hot and cold waterfalls (unbelievably awesome!). The treatments were also terrific. I think this may be the best spa in Israel and we are definitely going to come back. But, what I said before still stands: this is a spa built in the early 2000's and hasn't been renovated since. If you are just coming for the spa, the pricing is fine and I wouldn't hesistate. But if you are using the spa as a hotel guest, I expect more for this price point.  Bottom line: this is a very good hotel, but overpriced relative to what it is. This is hotel is priced as a 5-star. While it may have been that 25 years ago, it has not kept up. By today's standards, 4-stars is more reasonable. So.... unless you are specifically looking for a facility that feels closer in time to the historical Herod (he may have used the same gym equipment), you may find yourself like me having paid for a 5-star experience that you didn't quite get and then having to correct the online record to set things straight. (And also, no matter what you decide, I suggest you pass on the "free wine.") || Thank you very much for your feedback. I thought Purim was about happiness and this place didn’t have  that vibes terrible place for my first experience of Purim in Israel and being in Israel. || The team was friendly and polite. The room was modern and clean. I liked the DJ party that happened on the roof on Friday afternoon. Also, the Shabbat dinner is "a la carte" and is fantastic for the price!  There was an unpleasant smell at the entrance (probably from the flowers). The hotel is next to the club the "Chato", and on Saturday nights, we hear the music bass. There is no private parking. || Good small hotel in middle of north beach . Different rooms. We got quite a small room. Good breakfast . Sometimes there loud music from hotel restaurant. No lobby. Small roof top pool. There is restaurant (called MOOD) FOR DINNER. No hotel parking but there is free oarking place nearby || This hotel has no lobby, or any indoor sitting space at all except at the check in desk.|The only place there is to sit is outdoors on the roof, where the pool and bar are.||If you don't like loud music, or sitting outdoors in the eilat … || Not just an ordinary vacation, One of a kind boutique experience. The hotel design is absolutely beautiful, the environment in the pool area and the restaurant is amazing - offering top level dinner and breakfast. No kids allowed, which create chilled and fresh atmosphere, these are rare things to find in the area. Super recommended! || Thank you for beeing with us 🖤 …

Unfortunately, my experience at this hotel was far from good. I checked in in the morning, the room was only ready at 6:00 PM. When we first arrived, we were assigned a room of higher value, but later in the evening, when they finally called to say our room was ready, we were given a different and lower-category room instead. We were told that the original one had been unavailable for three days — like we invented that someone gave us this room.  The building is very old, and cleanliness is poor both inside the rooms and throughout the hotel. The gym is practically non-existent — dirty, abandoned, and it looks like no one has used or maintained it for years.  Another major issue is the parking. There are far too few parking spaces for the hotel’s capacity. Every night, coming back from dinner, I had to go in and out of the parking area multiple times, often getting stuck with other cars doing the same thing. The staff even told us to park outside, in an extra dirt parking lot, which is completely neglected and risky to drive into — and even that area was often blocked by other vehicles.  The quality of the food was very poor, often served cold. The only two positive things about my stay were the swimming pool, which has great potential, and the kindness of a security guard at the entrance, named Isa (if I remember correctly). For two nights in a row, seeing how tired and frustrated I was, he kindly offered me his parking spot — a really nice gesture, even though it shouldn’t be his responsibility to solve such issues.  Overall, this hotel needs serious improvement in management, maintenance, and service. The price is absolutely not justified for what you get. Very poor service and lack of organization. || We've truly enjoyed out stay at Orchid. We've arrived quite late (around 11pm) but the service was top. Talking to the service lady saying we're on a holiday to celebrate our 1 year anniversary, she was happy to try and upgrade our room, but couldn't. Just trying was nice!  Arriving to the hotel room, the AC was already on (nice touch), and the room wss clean and ready for our arrival (apart from someone's pills in one of the drawers, I must add).  The bathroom was really big with double sinks and double shower heads, but, since there was no curtains to stop the water from getting in to the center of the bathroom, everything was watery, we didn't enjoyed it all.  The breakfast was great! Many options ans types of food - from cereals to fishes to lasagna.  The pool was at the right temperature!! Not too hot, not too cold, with great view to the sea + baby pools.  On one of the occasions where we wanted to travel to the city (which was pretty far, about 15 minutes away) we met the service lady again, asking how we're enjoying the hotel and told her that everything is incredible. On our way back, a campaign has waited for us with two glasses...  It was an incredible visit (ar least for us). Thank you for having us! || Orchid is very nice place for family vacation. There are pools for any children's age. In opposite, it might be unacceptable for disable or old people. Non standard solution. Fantastic breakfast, etc. || We stay off season mid week and it was great. Beautiful rooms, tasty brakfest and nice stuff. We like the concept and the style of the hotel. Will come back || An Honest Review After 15 Years – This Will Definitely Be My Last Time! After 15 years of coming to this hotel every year, this time will be my very last visit. I booked a Shangri-La Villa, which is supposed to be the hotel’s VIP accommodation — but everything inside is broken and falling apart. There are ants in the room, the light switches don’t work, the electric curtains have been dead for years, and all the furniture is old and crumbling. The TV looks like it’s from before the state was founded, the shower pressure is extremely weak, and the dining room food is worse than an army base cafeteria. And all of this costs 2,500₪ per night — on a weekday, not even during a holiday! An absolute disgrace and shame. ‏ I have to say that the service from the stuff is very good, but it has nothing to do with the poor condition of the accommodations! || One Star. Horrible Stay From check-in to check-out, this hotel was a disaster. The room was filthy and uncomfortable. The staff were dismissive and offered no help. The amenities were broken or unavailable and the noise all night made it impossible to sleep. I left early and found another hotel. This place ruined my trip. Never again. || The place was cute and matched exactly what we needed. The kids enjoyed the food and the pool very much. The service was polite and pleasant. || Very peaceful place, with great energy. The entire staff are very friendly, and welcoming. Thank you for great weekend 🫶🙏 || This isn’t a 4 star hotel. Maybe 3 at best. The last time I was here was about 30 years ago and it is exactly the same as I remember it, which is to say the place clearly hasn’t been invested in or upgraded since. Stray cats absolutely … || Deserves a way better rating. I felt like I’m relaxing in Thailand. It’s nice it’s a 10min drive to center, it’s quiet and they provide bikes for free. Thank you to Patricia who was very helpful and kind.

A great viewpoint of Eilat and the Red Sea. We visited during sunrise, but for optimal photos, I suggest visiting for sunset. There is pleanty of parking around and it is free. What I didn't love about this viewpoint is all the houses that are between you and nature. || Its high up so you get a lovely view of the sunrise.Tbe mountains are also gorgeous. Probably sunset is also breathtaking. || Nice easy to get to viewpoint of Eilat and The Red Sea with plenty of parking space. || nice view over city of eilat and sea, with info board with voice  (!) hebrew and english explanation of the panorama... worth to visit even for locals to see the city from a different perspective... free parking and easy slope for wheelchairs and baby strollers BUT BUT BUT *not* to the very top of the observatioin desk, there are 20-25 wooden steps in groups of 3 and 4, manageable with strollers probably difficult with wheelchair, should give 4 stars || Very nice view point over Eilat and all around. You can even see Saudic Arabia. There's a switchable voice system on both Hebrew and English, explaining the objects you see from that spot. || Bresthtaking view of red sea n  gulf || Been there at night, great observation over the city area. Well maintained || Great viewing point to see all of Eilat || Excellent place to visit || Bring a coat it can get very windy

Very solid beach with beautiful coral reefs. Was super quiet when I went practically empty so was added bonus. Perfect for snorkelling and just general sunbathing. No water sports though. || The world northernmost coral reef, really! Right at your foot steps in eilat, Jordan has none. This beach has the advantage of not being overcrowded and all facilities are here, showers, toilets, bar, and a small nature reserve shop and rental services if you forgot your snorkeling equipment. Note, there are no lifeguard, only park rangers, but there is a space by the beach, in shallow water for poor swimmers Plant to bring some water shoes for the beach side. The reef is accessible via a long pier, and a large staircase leading easily to the water. Then it is the wonders of the red sea! || Although its one of the best places to see corals and fish in Eilat. The site could be a bit more developed. There are not many showers and only one dock to enter the water and relatively small place for swimming. With limited hours of operation and mediocre services this beautiful natural reserve should get an upgrade and the site could invest some of the entrance fee in improvments. || The reserve is well-maintained, clean, and organized, with food shops and equipment rental available. While the price is a bit high compared to free nearby spots, the underwater experience is spectacular- vibrant corals, colorful marine life, and plenty to see.  The area is very accessible, and safety is taken seriously with lifeguards on duty. Showers and restrooms are available and well-kept. Most seating areas are shaded with white canopies, which helps, though it can still get extremely hot in July and August.  Some downsides include ongoing renovations, which limit access to newer sections and make planning a snorkeling route a bit challenging. The designated swimming areas are small and enclosed, but beyond the bridge, there are vast open spaces where you can really explore and see a lot of beautiful marine life.  Overall, it’s more comfortable and enjoyable to snorkel in a well-supervised, maintained area than in unofficial sites, and the beautiful coral and abundant sea creatures make it well worth a visit.  * Pros: Clean and organized, lifeguards on duty, beautiful corals and marine life, showers and restrooms, accessible. * Cons: Entry fee is high compared to free alternatives, renovations limit some areas, enclosed swimming zones can feel small, it can get very hot in summer. || Snorkelling is ok. Nice fish and a bit of coral. If you've been in good reef places, you won't be impressed. But if in Eilat, it's worth a visit but a bit expensive for what it offers. || One of the good beaches in Eilat Clean,  had toilet,  shop,  walk route,  bridge directly to Red see with excitement view of corals, different fish types It's needed some payment,  check possible options before coming there It's better come with your own equipment Pay attention - NO SAFE GUARDS || Our preferred place in Eilat! Every time we are in Eilat we go to this place, the best still and ever.  Actually we were there every day, not a problem as we slept at the Yam Suf Hotel, only a 5 minute walk to there. 1. the beach is incredibly looked after 2. The Reserve guards are watching all the time for trespassers so very little chance something bad could happen to you while swimming 3. and of course the corals and the fish. Yes the coral are less beautiful than in the previous years, the mini tsunami a few years ago did damage the reef, but still they are interesting and the fish are till there and still super beautiful. Don't "FOMO" it, would you? || We had a lovely day out here. It was February, so out of season and not too busy. Lots of beautiful sea life up close in enormous tanks. Also, a very nice undersea viewing room and a sub trip if you want. Loads of facilities and other interesting things to see.....  Lovely and we'll worth a visit 😀 … || Amazing place! Make sure you take snorkels!  For 35 shekel, the place offers quite an experience! A long stretch of white sand, beautiful reefs to snorkel and pretty secure! || The most beautiful marine reserve in the world – colorful gardens beneath the sea The reefs of the Gulf of Eilat are the only coral reefs in our country, and among them a wonderful and colorful world of corals, fish and a huge variety of unique creatures can be seen. The Coral Beach Nature Reserve in Eilat allows visitors easy access to the reef, as well as essential beach services, including a shop, showers, toilets, sunshades, deck chairs and sun loungers

A real fun place for kids, but also for the sea animal lovers. We had a guided tour and it was perfect and well explained. I enjoyed every bit of it. I would have enjoyed more if the glasses were a bit cleaner. Nevertheless, it was fun. PS: The 3D movie was cherry on the top || Would spend there all day. An established place, but it keeps renovating all the time. The shark aquarium is so relaxing and exiting at the same time! The underwater observatory facility is a must. Note- a single ticket is good for a couple of days, so if you want to visit more than once (and you should) plan accordingly. || It is very expensive. The tanks are too small for the large number of fish and turtles. In addition, the glass on the tanks is dirty everywhere, making it difficult to see properly. This needs to be cleaned urgently. The grounds are small overall and half of the attractions consist of films. It is not a must-see. || Good for little kids, probably less for older ones.  The place is trying hard to remain relevant. The underwater observetory is a little old and not really that impressive anymore. However you also get an impressive shark pool and some stingray and sea turtles exhibits. The 3d movie was impressive (but short. 18 min total).  I've certainly been to better aquariums, but this is decent and good for kids. || Wonderful. From walking through the lively coral reef to the 3D cinema which is unlike any other I have witnessed. The screen goes above the head so that it can be protected from any point in the room and looks like the whole is above you. This place is a must see for young and old. It is a beautifully maintained park, with a big variety of coral. The underwater observatory is absolutely amazing. The water of the red see is also accommodating the coral beautifully. The aqua dome is also an experience like none other. The whole is turned into a 3D video and it literally feels like you are under the ocean and touching the sea life yourself. Great place to visit, both educational and fun. its really impressive to see all the unique creatures that live in the ocean. dedicate at least several hours to the visit. || This place gets it!  It's all about the service and people.  Incredibly helpful and friendly staff.  Very clean place.  Food was good and fair priced.  The exhibits were all well maintained.  Especially with children, this is a very nice all day activity. || We’ve been to aquariums all over the world and this isn’t the glossiest or the most high tech. But my kids love it and beg to come back every time we are in Eilat. There’s lots of different things to do that keep everyone entertained and you cannot beat seeing fish in their actual habitat. We love this charming little place. The 3-D movie was a huge hit! || What a great chance to sit and watch fish for hours! Between the underwater observatory and the aquarium we were really pleased with the experience.  Go early for quieter viewing without crowds. There was plenty of parking when they first opened. || We spent the whole day, ~7 hours, so there's lots to do there. I won't give it a 5 star since some things definitely need more love. We saw all the exhibits, there's really a good wide variety and selection of sea creatures, most endemic to Eilat. The highlight must be the shark tank, it has multiple viewing windows, plenty of room, probably the nicest tank I've seen. They feed them twice daily - go to the second feeding! (3pm) it far less crowded. There's a tube to walk under the fish and rays, beautiful. There are also turtles and "rare creatures" (which we didn't find very "rare"). The "deep sea creatures" exhibit is only videos. The lowest point must be the "IMAX", the movie is short, although the 3D effect is cool (kids loved it), but the narration (Heb only) is unintelligible, the content is boring, and they play a "generic" 3D flick. The underwater structure is very nice, but many windows are way too high for a 3-4 y/o to see anything without carrying them 💪, still it's very worth the while (climb up to see the overlook). It's a good place to spend a few hours, it doesn't break the bank, and kids will like it. || Great place to visit. Easy to get to by bus from Eilat. You can buy tickets online or at the gate. The exhibits are lovely.. sharks, stingrays, corals, turtles, octopi, fish. Climb the observatory to the top to see great views of the Red Sea.. then go below sea level to view coral and fish. Try and avoid Jewish / school holidays is it gets very busy. The 3D movie was an extra .. it was not so good.

Easy to get to, two separate balconies, great spot for sunrise! || Amazing view, a bit chilli at night || Beautiful view, the lighting there is too strong and it is difficult to see the surroundings. Unfortunately there is no disabled access. || Amazing view of the Red Sea and the city of Eilat A monthly meeting place for amateur astronomers who perform overnight parking and night observations every Rosh Chodesh and enjoy an amazing and breathtaking view in one of the darkest and most interesting places in the area. You can also reach by private car for lovers of the genre... Of course, you can also visit in the early morning and during the day when the temperatures are comfortable. A quiet and fun place for making outdoor coffee and taking a short break from the daily routine... Highly recommended! || 2 balconies with great views. Open 24/7 for free for the public. || Spectacular, at sunset and at night it has a view of all of Eilat and Jordan || Well-invested and beautiful. Parking nearby, beautiful both at night and during the day. || Recommended. This is an urban complex built for observation of the city of Eilat and the bay. 2 observation posts at the edge of a cliff, at the end there is a wide balcony suitable for dozens of people at the same time. The place is neat and organized, lit and invested in a proper and beautiful way. At the observation point there is an interactive map with audio in English and Hebrew explaining the viewing points from the observation point. At night the place is safe, lit and especially romantic. In the evenings it is recommended to arrive with a light windbreaker. || A charming view of Eilat, also a story about Eilat

Best suited for snorkeling.  Even if you don't know swimming you can  rent the snorkeling face  equipment and just use it next to the beach to view the amazing corals and beautiful fishes. || You might be able to peek here and there at the reef. Not the entire area is accessible to public. They have a 750m long lane accessible with bridges for swimming, snorkeling and scuba diving (bring your own gear- though they might rent if needed - at least snorkeling). Not really food option but it’s a nice bring your own food stay by the beach kind of place. There is a supermarket across from the road where parking is free and where you can get goodies.  Amenities are sparse but that is fine. || Amazing beach. So fun jumping off the deck! Really gorgeous views and access to marine life. Free beach and they offer lounge chairs and snacks! || Very cool beach, only with rocks and perfect for snorkeling and diving. Location well equipped with bar, umbrellas and deckchairs. || Great beach for snorkeling. Gear rental on site. Picnic tables, shade and food. || Heaven for snorkelling, especially for nervous snorkellers: they have designed a snorkelling 'route' around the reef with a rope you can use for guidance and feeling a bit more secure. The marine life is amazing with huge colourful fish. They rope of the main reef to protect it from damage from selfish tourists, but you can still see it from the edge. Beach has plenty of shade and chairs. All equipment and lockers available. Take your own food  as all you can get here are french fries or frozen pizza they heat up. You can get here by a 5 minute bus from the main area of Eilat. || Very well organized for snorkeling but maybe too much... in the water you can’t really get close to the corals and there are many people at the same place so not so wild as you could expect. || Great experience. Lots of space to sit. The snorkelling was great fun and there were lots and lots of fish. || Good facilities with snorkel hire, locker hire, shower, toilets etc. However, you have to view the coral in a guided lane, which is very restrictive. The coral is better in other places along the coast, but there was a decent variety of fish to see. || It's a place with shower, toilets, diving equipment to rent, shops and more. There public bus lines getting you from any point of Eilat to this Nature Reserve Beach. In Hebrew: חוף האלמוג Hof Halmog. The beach is huge and very clean. Wonderful for sea nature lovers because there you can see all the sea life just getting in the sea. The Red Sea waters are an spectacle for the clear swimming, good temperature and the lack of waves that allow you to see all the amazing under water life. The entrance is not free. You may need to call to know opening hours and entry ticket prices.

We came 5 mins after 12pm (and tickets are valid also tomorrow from the morning only! - as explained on the cash desk); spent some half day here late March; sea temperature fresh but still acceptable; not so crowded today; beach service collect beach chairs regularly; easy to find place and take chairs, we enjoy hot and cold sweets with coffee and fresh Mint lemonade. Really tasty; recommended; next time I repeat. || Amazing ! Such an incredible experience ! Staff are also amazing ! Estelle was great called me told me best times to come ! Mayaan was so welcoming and beautiful and IRa was amazing guide ! She was brilliant and supported me on my first dive ! Dolphins are everywhere ❤️❤️ || For the standard entrance fee you can swim at the beach and spend some time on the pier to film and shoot the dolphins (pier closes at 5 pm). Then you have a bar restaurant upstairs in a wonderful place (forbidden under 18 years old). From this place you still can see the dolphins, enjoy the sun and even stay until 11 pm! || Great place. We did snorkeling with the dolphins, it was great to see them in their natural habitat. Our instructor was a very nice and professional lady that took care of everyone’s comfort and made sure everyone is safe and have an amazing time. I was really scared of the depth but thanks to her I could overcome my fear and enjoy the moment. I can’t thank her enough. It’s a place one of a kind and people there are very welcoming. I highly recommend, worth every penny. || I had a great expirience to dive with dolphins..its something amazing..also the place its like heaven..its diferent than other places that i saw in Israel. The relaxing pools inside its something special too. I recommand everyone to visit. || Wonderful location, really worth the detour even though it's located on the other side of Eilat. There's also a bar inside where you can order drinks and bites. Service was great and the food was delicious. A big 5! || Very clean beach and not too crowded. Dolphins seem happy and free. Very good diving guides, and great service. They even offered us a refund for  for one who couldn't make it on time, because they had another person who was interested to dive instead. || Very beautiful dolphin reef. Tourist attraction. We saw 3 dolphins. The food here was delicious, totally recommend! There are also student fares for entry. || Dolphin Reef in Eilat is a natural habitat of Dolphins. We can observe the dolphins 🐬 from the floating bridge provided. The dolphins are very playful and you are allowed to touch them if you wish to.  The security staff watches over the dolphins as well as feeds them.Some snorkeling facility is also there. We visited long back. The Dolphin Reef is open from Monday to Saturday.  Timings: 9 am to 5 pm. We spent some time observing the dolphins.  There is an entry fee. || The most wonderful beach in Eilat. It’s like a completely different world everything beautiful and clean and pleasant. The food at the beach restaurant is great. And to watch the dolphins is certainly a bonus 🐬 …

We visited the park with my family and our children were excited to see so many fish here. Also we floated a boat and saw underwater reef life || Very very good for visit with kids for full day joing! || Great place, especially for children. We really enjoyed the observatory and the boat👌 … || It lifetime memorable moments here || Good experience, the prices at the dinary are really high , for ice cream you will pay 14 nis (regular price is 10/9), for ice water you will pay 16 (regular price is 5-10) The exhibits are magicl , I really recommend. The boat/submarine cost 40 nis and the duration of the ship is 15 min. || A wonderful place with tons of entertainment for adults and kids. The Aquadome is worth adding to your ticket. || Nice place for family with kids- during the day, several events- including feeding the sharks, tortils.... || Amazing place, rare fish and sharks. Huge aquariums and much more!! Very recommended || Very good for kids. Many activities.

The statues of the caravan to Mecca. Beautiful metal statues showing the caravan of the committee to Mecca. All the statues look identical and are about 100 meters long, behind the caravan is the image of a beautiful mosque. Worth coming and being impressed.

Not far from the birds observatory, they can instruct you there how to find the place since its can be a bit tricky. definitely worth a visit. In our visit on March we saw 3 Lizards. || We were there in early July. They suggested coming when it was hot. So it was hot. Very hot. We walked around for half an hour in 44 degrees and didn't see a single skunk. It seems like the place isn't maintained. A waste of time || Amazing. It's hard to see them. It's recommended to arrive at the peak of the heat. || Strange. We were there in early December, at the end of a day that was all sunny, about an hour before sunset. We didn't see a single hawk. It was inconspicuous and strange. If we weren't looking for time to burn and came specifically, it would have been extremely annoying. According to the maps, the access road is blocked, we got around with interesting car crossings along the way, but that was the only fun. || A well-maintained and well-maintained place. Free entry. Arrived on an unpaved dirt road. Unfortunately, I did not see any hawksbills. Later I was told that in fact you can see hawksbills starting in May. || You should be careful with your vehicle, the trail is not really well-maintained. However, it is a lovely place! It is recommended to arrive at the peak of the heat. || Unfortunately I didn't see any roaches. Unpaved road with deep potholes. The bottom of my car was dented. || We went there twice at different times of day. Unfortunately, we only saw a lizard once, briefly, and otherwise nothing at all. There's also a lot of trash lying around. || A strange place, although with patience we spotted giant ants. No good intentions || Amazing animals to see, right next to all the usual attractions in Eilat, an option for a slightly different attraction, highly recommended

place_name: International Birding and Research Center Eilat
reviews_content: A local centre in Eilat (5km north of the city) focused on the studying and helping of migratory birds that pass from Eurasia to Africa (and back).  Open 24/7, free entrance. BUT! Call in advance to book a local, very experienced, guide that will take you around (mandatory). 35 shekel per person or 100 per family. || Thank you very much, we appreciate your kind words and very happy you enjoyed your visit. || Very peaceful trail, nice place to take family. The employees in the center were overwhelmingly friendly when we went. I also follow the center on FB and they post great bird photos. Really loved this place at sunset, will recommend to anyone traveling to Eilat. || The most important goal of this station is to ensure the well being and safe passage of birds migrating. Dedicated staff and volunteers. || The place looks well equipped with different habitats and nice hides but when we went in late September 2019 only one hide was accessible, the rest were closed off due to construction work and the place was deserted, with no staff around. We saw a few common waders during our visit one afternoon. || It is such an important station for migratory birds. We have not seen too many birds, since January is not the season for migration, but we still enjoyed the tranquility of the place,  took a nice stroll around and read the information that are displayed all over the place. I am looking forward to returning during migration season. || We had a privat guided tour - it was really great and we learned a lot about bird migration! || The entrance is free, and the place itself is tranquil, as it should be. You can see many locals going for a silent job in the morning, enjoying the view and the singing of birds that come to eat, or simply living here. It is not common to have a guided tour, but it will be worth it if you manage to book one. Also, you should bring or rent a binocular. || Internationally important. Hundreds of millions of birds visit the center in spring and autumn. Here they find resources to continue their migration. Come when the center is most active and come in the early morning to see the most. (This is no zoo; everything is wild and free.) || Very interesting and educational. They said it was the second largest bird sanctuary in the world . I was given a free lecture and tour around the sanctuary. I had an enjoyable couple of hours there. || Wetlands with many blinds to observe birds from. In the morning you can see the staff band migratory birds.

A high end quality food restaurant, and a great brewery. I recommend the ceviche and carpaccio. Make sure to ask about the beer of the month, it was a great surprise! || Michael, thank you so much for the amazing review! We’re thrilled you enjoyed the ceviche, carpaccio and of course our Soof beer. Glad the Beer of the Month surprised you, we put a lot of love into it 😊 Hope to see you again soon! … || The food is meh. There's a vast selection in the menu which was immediately a red flag. The fried cauliflower was a bit burned. The bangers & mash was simply merguez/chorizo (nothing like bangers) on potato puree with demi-glace/BBQ sauce (instead of the traditional onion gravy). I ordered the beer tasting flight, and the beers are alright. As an IPA lover I didn't really like their IPA at all, but I did like the wheat beer and the Thaistory limited edition beer. Our friends mentioned a weird smell when walking into the restaurant. The music that was playing in the restaurant was nice. || Hello Amit, thanks for the review.  Regarding the IPA, it's a style that has a very personal taste; many IPA fans like ours, you probably didn't connect as much, and that's natural. We'll check the smell at the entrance immediately to make sure there's nothing unusual.  Thank you for your honesty, and we'll be happy to host you again for a better experience. || Went with the kids on a Saturday night. We ordered several starters (chicken wings, fried cauliflower, onion rings) and several entrees (Cesar salad, three types of pasta for the kids and a hamburger) as well as an assortment of beers. The beers were quite good and the starters went down well. The salad and pastas were mediocre, but that's to be expected of a place that specializes in beer and meat.  After all the entrees arrived and everyone was finished eating I asked our waiter if the hamburger would be making an appearance. They forgot about it. Well, that happens. I was told that it would be free and they'll immediately prepare it. I can live with that.  Twenty minutes later, it had still failed to make an appearance, although at least seven other burgers successfully made it out. They forgot it a second time! I asked for the bill... || Hi Gilad, Thank you very much for your review and for sharing with us what happened tonight.  We sincerely apologize that the burger did not arrive – tonight was unusually busy, especially since it was the eve of Tisha B’Av, and we are among the only restaurants in the city that were open. Unfortunately, the order was missed – and this is not something we take lightly.  We would be very happy to compensate you with two burgers and two appetizers at home – either sitting in with us or by delivery, whichever is convenient for you.  You are welcome to contact me personally at 054-6333903 or directly to the restaurant at 050-5595576 – and we will make sure that you receive the compensation you deserve.  Best regards, Natan – Owner Eilat Brewery 🍻 || You have to come here!!! Food is incredible, drinks also, and service efficient and so friendly.  We arrived at 8pm on Friday night (Shabbat), they initially said they didn’t have any tables until late but we’d been driving for hours through the desert and I asked once more and they tried their absolute best to fit us in to our relief. Everyone was so accommodating, food was incredible (my partner said the best steak he’s ever had) and the beef stew is unreal, cannot recommend this place enough. I didn’t have their beer this time but I’ve also had it before and it’s amazing. Don’t miss eating out here if you come to Eilat! || Thank you so much for your kind words and for sharing your experience 🙏 We’re really happy we could make you feel comfortable after such a long drive, and that you enjoyed the food and atmosphere. Your compliments to the team and the dishes truly warm our hearts ❤️  We look forward to welcoming you again on your next visit to Eilat 🍻  The Brewery Team || Lovely restaurant, great for family lunch and at night for a bar. Caffe Optimi was the perfect place for a very special family celebration, and we couldn’t have chosen better.  We came as a large family gathering, with relatives visiting all the way from Byron Bay, Australia and Boston, USA, to celebrate our son’s Bar Mitzvah — and from the moment we arrived, we felt completely welcomed.  The atmosphere was warm, relaxed, and joyful, exactly what you want for a meaningful family occasion. The food was outstanding: the pizza was absolutely amazing 🤩, fresh, flavorful, and clearly made with care, and the hot chocolate was divine 🤤 — rich, comforting, and unforgettable.  What truly elevated the experience, though, was the people. Our waiter Idan was attentive, kind, and genuinely lovely. And Ofer, the manager, was so friendly, welcoming, and present. You can tell he truly cares about both his guests and his team, and that warmth fills the entire place.  This is what our son had to say, and honestly, it says it all:  “The pizza was amazing 🤩, the hot chocolate was divine 🤤, and the staff was nice. If I could give this place more stars, I would.”  If you’re looking for a café with great food, wonderful service, and a heart big enough to hold special moments and celebrations — Caffe Optimi is it. place_name: משהו מתבשל פה - מסעדה כשרה באילת
reviews_content: We arrived in Eilat, both of us hungry. We searched Google for a good cooking restaurant. And we discovered the restaurant Something's Cooking Here. Delicious, fresh food, excellent service, a plate full of heart. I'll definitely come here every time I come to Eilat. || I had a really positive experience with this catering service. The moment I arrived, I was impressed by the wide selection of freshly prepared food, all neatly displayed and giving off that warm, home-style Shabbat feeling.  Personally, I chose schnitzels, mini challah rolls, juicy grilled chicken ("pargiot"), potatoes, and delicious fish patties. Everything tasted fresh, flavorful, and well-prepared. The schnitzels were crispy and perfect for the kids, the pargiot were tender and seasoned just right, and the fish patties had that homemade quality you don’t usually find in catering. The challah rolls were soft, fresh, and really added to the Shabbat table.  Even though these were the dishes I took, I noticed there’s also a much bigger variety available – beef dishes, different types of rice, vegetables, stuffed bourekas, and more. It’s clear that no matter what your preferences are, you can find plenty of options.  Another big advantage is the packaging. The food is arranged in individual plastic containers so you can pick exactly what you want in manageable portions. They also have aluminum trays, which are perfect for placing directly on the Shabbat hot plate. It made preparing for Shabbat much more convenient.  The service was excellent – very friendly, quick, and helpful. Despite the Friday morning rush, the atmosphere was pleasant and organized, and I was able to get everything I needed without waiting too long.  As for the price, I paid around 350 NIS for enough food to cover two adults and two kids, with plenty left for the next day. Considering the quality, convenience, and variety, I think it’s very fair.  Another important point is the kosher certification – Glatt kosher under Rabbi Mahpud. That gives a lot of confidence and peace of mind, especially when preparing food for Shabbat.  Pros:  Fresh and tasty food (schnitzels, pargiot, potatoes, fish patties, challah rolls were all excellent)  Wide variety of additional options available  Convenient packaging (plastic containers and aluminum trays)  Friendly, efficient service  Fair pricing for generous portions  Strict Glatt kosher supervision  Cons:  On Fridays, food sells out quickly – best to arrive early (before 10:00 AM).  Overall, I was very satisfied. The food was delicious, the service was smooth, and the whole experience made getting ready for Shabbat much easier. Highly recommended! || Wonderful place! Great food excellent customer service very little waiting time excellent excellent customer service pretty cheap... || Great food. Good hechsher. Top service. The staff are incredibly attentive and friendly, making sure you’re comfortable without ever being intrusive.  The food is the real highlight. Every dish feels thoughtfully prepared and full of flavor. The fresh pasta stands out — perfectly cooked, rich sauces, and generous portions that still feel balanced. The seafood dishes are especially impressive, with ingredients that taste fresh and well-seasoned. The pizzas are also excellent, with a thin, crispy crust and high-quality toppings.  Service is surprisingly fast considering how busy the restaurant often is, and everything arrives hot and beautifully plated. The menu has great variety, so both picky eaters and adventurous diners will find something they love.  Prices are on the higher side, but absolutely justified for the quality and overall experience. Pastory is the kind of place you look forward to returning to — a reliable, flavorful, and memorable spot in Eilat. Highly recommended for couples, families, and anyone who appreciates great Italian food. || The place itself was pleasant, and I was glad we were seated outside. Overall, it remains one of the most activity-rich hotels in Eilat, but the standards decline each year and might no longer fully justify the price.  Room cleanliness was disappointing. We were upgraded from a Superior U room (the most basic category) to a balcony room, but the upgrade was not worthwhile. Last time we stayed in the Superior U room, and to me it felt newer, cleaner, and had a much nicer bathroom than the balcony room. The balcony room’s bathroom was very small, with a combined tub/shower and only a half glass partition, so water splashed everywhere. The Superior U bathroom, while shower-only, is more spacious and modern. In the balcony room, the tub felt old and not properly cleaned, there was hair on the bed, the sofa bed was opened without request, and there was no water or welcome package in the room..  I would not recommend staying during a storm. Check the weather! The power went out for about half an hour, and roads into and out of Eilat were closed. Reception handled this well and graciously offered us an additional night at a slightly discounted rate (around 10%), which we declined. Instead, they offered a complimentary dinner pass, which was much appreciated.  The food remains a strong point. Dinner was excellent, with a wide and impressive variety: steaks, asado, pulled beef bao buns, schnitzel, chicken dishes, and more. The variety is consistently very good. Breakfast, however, was underwhelming. Limited selection, poor pastries, mediocre orange juice, and only black and green tea available.  The dairy restaurant is very good, but availability is limited to certain days and requires first-come, first-served sign-up. Arriving early is essential.  Unlimited cocktails are fun, but the bar offering is basic. Mostly straight liquors with fruit juices. The slushies are extremely sweet and artificial. Bartender skill varies significantly, though one bartender managed to make a decent piña colada. Drinks are always served in plastic cups, though glass cups can be requested at the indoor bar.  Snorkel rentals and beach equipment are excellent. However, windsurfing is advertised but never seems to happen. On multiple visits there has always been an excuse. This time we were told the instructor had passed away...  I would go again, mainly because no other hotel in Eilat offers this level of activities and programming.
